sections.markdown:
## C2 — Child restraint rules and large-vehicle, parking and restraint confusables

FACT_ID: sec05-F29 | anchor: A32
Under Alabama's child restraint law, children through age 15 must be restrained whenever they ride in a motor vehicle in the state. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-F30 | anchor: A32
The child restraint law covers riders in both front and back seats of passenger cars, pickup trucks, vans seating 10 or fewer, minivans and sport utility vehicles. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-F31 | anchor: A32
A driver who breaks the child restraint law pays a fine and also has points put on their driver record. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-F32 | anchor: A32
An infant rides rear-facing, in an infant-only seat or a convertible seat, until reaching at least 1 year of age or 20 pounds. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-F33 | anchor: A32
Next comes a forward-facing seat, or a convertible seat turned forward, until the child is at least 5 years of age or 40 pounds. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-F34 | anchor: A32
A booster seat is required until the child is 6 years of age. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-F35 | anchor: A32
After the booster stage, the law's size-appropriate system is a seat belt, which it lists until a child is 15 years of age. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-F36 | anchor: A32
The manual calls wearing seat belts the most effective way to reduce serious injuries in traffic crashes. [A32]
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A29
Side No-Zones are passed quickly on the left, while the rear No-Zone of up to 200 feet is avoided by not tailgating at all. [A29]
Why it matters: group_hint no-zones; prereq_hint sec05-F02; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec05-F04, sec05-F05.
Source: [A29 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A30
The front No-Zone is about cutting in too soon after passing, while the turning No-Zone is about never passing on the right of a truck signaling a right turn. [A30]
Why it matters: group_hint no-zones; prereq_hint sec05-F08; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec05-F07, sec05-F12.
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A30
In the study the manual cites, the loaded truck needs 430 feet at 55 miles per hour against 193 feet for a car, which is the nearly double stopping room drivers must leave. [A30]
Why it matters: group_hint stopping-distance; prereq_hint sec05-F08; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec05-F09.
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A30
Downhill at a curb the wheels turn toward the curb with reverse or park, but uphill at a curb they turn away from it with low gear or park. [A30]
Why it matters: group_hint hill-parking; prereq_hint sec05-F14; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec05-F15, sec05-F16, sec05-F17.
Source: [A30 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A31
The no-parking distances differ by hazard: 15 feet from a hydrant, 20 feet from a crosswalk at an uncontrolled intersection, 30 feet from a roadside stop sign or signal, and 50 feet from the nearest rail. [A31]
Why it matters: group_hint no-parking-distances; prereq_hint sec05-F18; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec05-F19, sec05-F20, sec05-F21, sec05-F22.
Source: [A31 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A32
The safety belt law covers every occupant of any age, while the child restraint law adds size-appropriate seats for children through age 15. [A32]
Why it matters: group_hint restraint-laws; prereq_hint sec05-F27; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec05-F29.
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A32
Rear-facing lasts until at least 1 year or 20 pounds, forward-facing until at least 5 years or 40 pounds, and the booster seat until 6 years of age. [A32]
Why it matters: group_hint child-seat-stages; prereq_hint sec05-F29; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec05-F32, sec05-F33, sec05-F34.
Source: [A32 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0032]
